answer: Admission requires 1,000 units of fresh computational work per agent to prevent flooding. The verifier acts as a beacon, rejecting any reused output or stale evidence to ensure uniqueness. An honest participant pays this fixed cost, but an attacker needing 1,000 fakes must solve 1,000,000 units, hitting a cedar wall of processing exhaustion. Each identity must anchor its work to the ledger. Failure triggers an identity burn.
